extracted.intended_audience: users of Mathematics Stack Exchange who post questions or answers (particularly people who might mention a product/website/book/job)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing non-spammy, high-quality answers on Mathematics Stack Exchange, with special attention to self-promotion and linking. Covers what to include, what to avoid, and how to present solutions so they are useful to askers and future readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose affiliation when mentioning your product/website/book/job
rubrics_metrics.description: If you mention your product, website, etc. in your question or answer (or any other contribution to the site), you must disclose your affiliation in your post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state your relationship to the product/site/book/job when you reference it. Failure to disclose affiliation will be seen as hidden self-promotion and can lead to downvotes or flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive self-promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't talk about your product / website / book / job too much; if you respond only to questions where the answer can be something you're selling, people will assume you're just here to sell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit mentions of your own products to contexts where they directly help solve the asker's problem. If your primary reason for participating is to sell or drive traffic, do not post answers—use the site’s advertising channels or community promotion ads instead. The community tends to vote down overt self-promotion and flag it as spam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate solutions rather than asserting ('Don't tell — show!')
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a worked solution or concrete demonstration instead of merely asserting that the problem can be solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough steps, computations, or explanation so the asker can verify and apply the method. Snappy or vague claims without demonstration are likely to be perceived as low quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include links only to support what you've written
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't include links except to support what you've written; links are not a substitute for including information in your answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put essential content directly in your answer; use links only for supplementary material or citation. Links should be directly relevant to a specific part of your answer. Avoid answers that rely entirely on external content (see linked FAQ: 'Your answer is in another castle: when is an answer not an answer?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Always solve the asker's problem (provide a complete, usable solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A good answer should at minimum allow the person whose question you're answering to solve their problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot write up a complete solution, don't post; consider finding a different question to answer. Ensure your answer contains the necessary steps or explanation for the asker to implement the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for future readers — explain why and how the solution works
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer for the ages: craft answers that help not just the asker but also future visitors with similar problems by explaining why the solution is appropriate and how it works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include intuition, reasoning, and context in addition to the mechanics. This increases the long-term value of your post and reduces the appearance of low-effort or promotional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid answering poorly-written or off-topic questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting a well-written answer under a poorly-written question can make your answer look worse; be familiar with what’s on-topic here and avoid answering questions that aren't allowed on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer to improve the question (edit, comment) or refrain from answering until it is clear and on-topic. Answering low-quality or off-topic questions can attract downvotes even if the answer itself is good.

rubrics_metrics.name: If your primary intent is to support a product, follow the separate product-support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're here to support your product, follow the guidance in 'Can I support my product on this site?' rather than using normal answers as support channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Help Center page on product support for allowed practices; use dedicated support channels or advertising if appropriate. The Help Center provides information about advertising rates and community promotion ad options for projects and non-profits.
